details: Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly involving the United States and Iran near the Strait of Hormuz, have intensified, leading to a significant surge in Brent crude oil prices, which have topped $100 to $110 a barrel. This escalation, combined with concerns over US inflation data and outflows from Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), is fueling risk aversion in global financial markets. Consequently, Bitcoin and other riskier assets are experiencing downward pressure, with crypto prices declining further. The situation is also impacting European energy markets, raising concerns about gas supplies for the upcoming winter.
sourceName: Economies.com (also reported by Pluang, INN, and ESMA)
title: Escalating Middle East Conflict Pushes Oil Prices Up, Bitcoin Down

details: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde has underscored the critical importance of developing a digital euro to ensure European sovereignty and control over its digital payment infrastructure. She warned that Europe must maintain command over how digital payments circulate. The ECB launched a two-year investigation phase in October 2021 to design and distribute a digital euro, considering its market impact and necessary legislative changes.
title: Lagarde: Digital Euro Key for European Sovereignty in Payments

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has highlighted that ongoing discussions between the United States and China are advantageous not only for the two major economies but also for global economic stability. Cooperation between the world's two largest economies is crucial for worldwide growth and stability, whereas confrontation could lead to slower global growth and disruptions in supply chains.
title: IMF: US-China Dialogue Positive for Global Economic Stability
